title: Cosmic Potato Benchmark — Laniakea as a Triaxial Kinematic Ellipsoid
status: archive-generated quantitative descendant of the Great Book Cosmic Potato morphology idea using current Laniakea kinematic literature; not evidence of universal potato morphology
purpose: Promote the scientifically strongest part of the historical Cosmic Potato intuition from visual resemblance to a measurable local-cosmography problem. Instead of asking whether Laniakea 'looks like a potato', model the dynamically selected Laniakea region as a triaxial ellipsoidal cell with an anisotropic velocity-gradient tensor and test whether that compact model predicts directional peculiar-velocity/luminosity-distance structure.
why_promising: Laniakea is now analyzed in the literature using an ellipsoidal peculiar-velocity model with principal-axis expansion/shear. This gives the project a genuine tensor observable and a model-comparison route. The scientific content is the triaxial kinematics and residual morphology, not the word potato.
epistemic_boundary: An ellipsoid is a generic low-parameter geometric model. Good ellipsoidal fits do not uniquely identify a potato/tuber morphology, universal scale law or Potatoverse mechanism. The project-specific contribution must come from a predeclared morphology/kinematics statistic that beats simpler alternatives.

kinematic_model.local_velocity_field: v_i(x)=v0_i + E_ij (x_j-x0_j) as a first-order affine approximation inside the selected region
kinematic_model.shear_tensor: sigma_ij=E_(ij) - (theta/3) delta_ij after removing any antisymmetric/vorticity component used in the chosen model
kinematic_model.principal_frame: Diagonalize the symmetric velocity-gradient tensor to obtain principal directions and eigen-expansion rates Delta H_a, Delta H_b, Delta H_c.
kinematic_model.interpretation: The ellipsoid is kinematic: its axes organize anisotropic flow/expansion. It need not coincide exactly with an isodensity solid or a uniquely bounded material object.

published_laniakea_reference_values.source_context: Values quoted in the 2026 supernova reconstruction as the Cosmicflows-4 ellipsoidal reference model it aims to recover.
published_laniakea_reference_values.trace_check: The shear eigenvalues sum approximately to zero within rounding, as required for a traceless shear tensor.
published_laniakea_reference_values.derived_anisotropy_indicator: Using A_sigma=sqrt[(3/2) sum_i sigma_i^2]/|theta| gives about 1.08 from the central values. This is an archive-derived dimensionless summary, not a standard published Laniakea statistic.
published_laniakea_reference_values.interpretation: The anisotropic shear is comparable in magnitude to the mean local expansion/contraction signal, so a spherical one-parameter description discards substantial directional structure.

potato_morphology_upgrade.old_question: Do plotted superclusters resemble rounded/oblong potatoes?
potato_morphology_upgrade.new_question: Does a compact triaxial ellipsoid plus controlled boundary roughness/topology provide a better low-complexity description of a dynamically defined region than sphere, filament/skeleton or unconstrained shape models?
potato_morphology_upgrade.candidate_descriptor: P_shape=(q=b/a, s=c/a, F_filamentarity, P_planarity, chi, R_surface, A_sigma)

components.F_filamentarity: dimensionless shapefinder from Minkowski functionals under a declared convention

potato_morphology_upgrade.rule: No single component is 'potatoness'. Predefine a compact/triaxial/low-filamentarity region in this descriptor space before evaluating a target.

model_comparison.H_sphere: isotropic spherical region/flow with one local expansion parameter
model_comparison.H_ellipsoid: triaxial ellipsoid with principal-axis expansion rates
model_comparison.H_watershed: nonparametric dynamical basin boundary obtained from reconstructed velocity streamlines
model_comparison.H_potato: ellipsoidal core plus a small, penalized irregular-boundary component and predeclared morphology bounds
model_comparison.success_rule: The project-specific H_potato is scientifically useful only if its added boundary/morphology structure improves held-out velocity/distance or shape statistics enough to justify its extra parameters over H_ellipsoid/watershed.

observables: 3D galaxy/group or reconstructed-density coordinates when testing geometry
watershed membership under the chosen velocity reconstruction
Minkowski functionals/shapefinders of a declared thresholded region

current_external_findings.2024_effective_model: A Cosmicflows-4-based study reports that Laniakea can be effectively described as an ellipsoid with triaxial expansion and that local anisotropic flow can shift inferred luminosity distances by percent-level amounts along different lines of sight.
current_external_findings.2026_supernova_reconstruction: A July 2026 arXiv study develops an independent supernova-based reconstruction of the ellipsoidal peculiar-velocity field and reports that luminosity-distance multipoles carry information about Laniakea expansion/shear and principal directions.
current_external_findings.important_caution: The exact amplitudes depend on geometry, centering, frame and data/model choices. This makes geometry-selection/systematic tests part of the model rather than an afterthought.

what_this_model_can_explain_if_successfu: Why local low-redshift distance/velocity residuals depend on direction through a triaxial peculiar-velocity field.
Why a spherical local-environment correction can miss substantial shear structure.
Whether the historical compact/oblong intuition can be reformulated as a quantitatively useful low-parameter morphology rather than a visual analogy.
what_it_does_not_explain: A universal potato shape across all cosmic scales.
A fundamental new force or dimension.
Why unrelated biological or quantum structures should share the same morphology.
next_calculations: Recover the published Laniakea ellipsoid semi-axis lengths/orientation and compute q,s with uncertainties.
Reproduce A_sigma and propagate covariance rather than using central values only.
Compare spherical versus triaxial velocity models on a public peculiar-velocity/supernova subset.
Compute geometry descriptors for the watershed boundary and compare with best-fit ellipsoid and filament models.
Define any project-specific irregular 'potato' residual before inspecting the held-out morphology so the test cannot adapt to every shape.
failure_conditions: The triaxial model fails to improve predictive likelihood over a spherical/local-flow baseline after complexity is penalized.
A filament/watershed representation consistently describes the selected object better than a compact ellipsoid-like one.
The inferred morphology is unstable under reasonable Cosmicflows reconstruction, threshold, centering or survey-selection changes.
The project calls any triaxial ellipsoid a potato without an independent predeclared discriminator.
